newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: Wienerberger 9-mth profit down, no upturn in sight.
newsitem.headline: Wienerberger 9-mth profit down, no upturn in sight.

text.p: Wienerberger Baustoffindustrie AG, the world's biggest brickmaker, reported a 20 percent drop in nine-month profit on Thursday and analysts held out scant hope of an early upturn in Europe's troubled building sector.

Austria's Wienerberger said nine-month pre-tax profit slumped to 1.041 billion schillings ($97.2 million) from 1.303 billion and promptly shaved its full-year earnings forecast to 1.2-1.4 billion schillings from 1.4 billion previously.

"But the original 1.4 billion schillings is still within reach," chief executive Erhard Schaschl told journalists, pinning his hopes on 100 million schillings from real estate sales by the end of the fourth quarter.
Wienerberger posted a pre-tax profit of 1.495 billion schillings last year.

"Construction is in the doldrums and there is no pick-up in sight. There probably won't be an upturn next year but it could come in 1998," said Robin Horne, Austria analyst at Kleinwort Benson in London.
"I am not suprised at all by the figures. The industry is going through its worst spell since the late 1980s," said Victoria Maxwell, an analyst at James Capel.

A severe winter across much of Europe coupled with sluggish construction have eroded Wienerberger's margins this year but an acquisition drive in France and Belgium has gone some way to keeping last year's profit figure in sight.

Wienerberger said its 1995 and 1996 acquisitions, France's Tuileries Reunies de Bas-Rhin (Sturm) and Belgium's Terca Bricks, would contribute some 430 million schillings to group pre-tax profit this year.
Terca -- Belgium's biggest brick maker bought by Wienerberger in April -- would account for around 350 million schillings of the total, Wienerberger said.
Analysts agreed that Wienerberger was well placed to benefit from an eventual upturn in European construction.
"Wienerberger is one of the most efficient operators in the industry," said Horne.
To the end of September the group reported an 11.6 percent rise in sales to 11.657 billion schillings and a 5.7 percent decline in earnings before interest and tax to 1.32 billion schillings.
The biggest downturn was in Wienerberger's wall, ceiling and roofing systems operations, where pre-tax profit slumped 36.7 percent to 540 million schillings.
"That was the main disappointment," said a Vienna bourse trader. "But overall the results were in line with expectations."
Wienerberger shares were trading 20.6 schillings at 1,980.5 early afternoon in a generally weaker market.
"I would not recommend Wienerberger as a "buy" at the moment. There will be better performing stocks in Vienna over the next year," Horne said. ($ = 10.70 Austrian Schillings)
